case.summary: Investigation into card C13190-K2 following an analyst alert for shared device profiles. Transaction 3562068 for $199.93 on 2016-12-21 was conducted via a MacOS device profile shared with four other cards in a one-week window. A broader scan identified a cluster of 8 cardholders and 16 transactions totaling $3,949.84 linked by two specific device profiles. Given the coordination and similarity to prior confirmed fraud cases like CC-3667, the activity is classified as card-not-present fraud.

sar.narrative: Between 2016-12-11 and 2016-12-31, a coordinated series of 16 online transactions totaling $3,949.84 was identified across 8 cardholders. On 2016-12-21, card C13190-K2 was used for a $199.93 purchase (ID 3562068) using a MacOS device profile. This specific device profile was also used by four other cards, including C01519-K1 and C02222-K1, to attempt similar amounts between 2016-12-19 and 2016-12-25. A connected-components scan revealed that these cardholders were further linked by a second shared device, an iOS profile. The MacOS device profile was seen on only 6 cards in six months, yet 4 of those cards showed high-risk activity within a single week. This pattern of multiple unrelated cardholders sharing the same hardware for online purchases is highly suspicious. Similar activity involving shared device profiles was previously confirmed as fraud in cases CC-3667 and CC-1356. The bank has blocked card C13190-K2 and placed connected cards under monitoring to prevent further loss. This report is filed because the activity connects to a shared device profile and coordinated abuse across multiple accounts.
